claim: GitHub made enterprise open-source license compliance generally available with merge rules and policy APIs.
verifiedFacts: GitHub's October 16 changelog announces general availability for GitHub Enterprise Cloud repositories with Code Security enabled.
The feature adds enterprise license rulesets, pull-request dependency annotations, policy audit events, and an API that can help coding agents avoid noncompliant packages.
inference: Inference: license review should become a separate supply-chain evidence boundary alongside vulnerability scanning and workflow pinning.
Consultancy implication: provide dependency-policy readiness assessment; client problem is agent-added dependencies with unreviewed license obligations.
Disposition: Seed Loom CORE and MelodicBloom governance CONSOLIDATE candidate; feature eligibility on these repos not established.
Thesis: extends CI assurance to licensing, not a replacement for security tests or legal review.
significance: A new enterprise enforcement surface creates a testable compliance workflow relevant to governed code generation and reproducible handoffs.
assumptions: Relevant clients operate eligible GitHub Enterprise Cloud repositories.
License metadata and exception governance are sufficiently complete for policy enforcement.
knownLimitations: Feature not verified as available on the user's repositories.
License compliance is not equivalent to vulnerability safety or legal advice.
